title: CQRS and event sourcing: reading and writing through different models

videos.script: Most applications keep one model of their data, and use it for everything. The same tables take the orders and answer every question about them. {{one}} That works until the two jobs start to want different things. Writes want rules and consistency. Reads want speed and shapes that suit each screen. {{two}} CQRS is the name for giving them separate models. One model takes the commands; others, built for reading, answer the queries. {{cqrs}} Event sourcing goes a step further. It stores not the current state of an order but every change that ever happened to it, and works out the state by replaying them. {{es}} On your machine you will build both, on one PostgreSQL. An order that is never updated, only appended to. A read model built from its events, which you can delete and rebuild. {{lab}} You will read an order as it was an hour ago, answer a question nobody planned for, and see two people change the same order at once. {{history}} And then the costs, because event sourcing has real ones, and most systems should not pay them.
